data.title: Show HN: I built an open-source tool to replace our internal analytics stack
data.text: We built this tool after spending years stitching together Google Analytics, Mixpanel, BigQuery and several internal scripts. It provides event tracking, funnels, retention analysis and a SQL interface. It is open source and self-hosted.

comments.text: This is really interesting. I've been looking for something like this.
We tried doing something similar, but getting our historical data into it was a nightmare.
The biggest problem for us is that there doesn't seem to be a good way to migrate years of Mixpanel data.
Yeah, we ended up writing our own Python importer because none of the tools we evaluated handled our custom event properties.
This is exactly the kind of thing I've wanted.
Our analysts also need scheduled reports emailed to stakeholders every Monday, so we'd need that before replacing our current setup.
Does it support scheduled reports?
We have about 20 million events per day. I'm wondering how expensive it gets at that scale.
The SQL interface is built on DuckDB, so query performance should be pretty good.
The technical architecture is fascinating.
We currently have to export data to CSV and upload it into BigQuery manually because our existing analytics vendor doesn't expose all the data through its API.
If this could sync the raw events to BigQuery automatically, that would save us several hours every week.
I've used a few of these and they all feel basically the same.
Why doesn't it just replace Google Analytics?
It would be great if there were a way to define retention cohorts using arbitrary SQL instead of only the UI filters.
We have non-technical marketing people creating dashboards, so the current SQL-based workflow is too difficult for them.
I don't understand why anyone would pay for another analytics tool.
This reminds me of a project I built in college.
We need role-based permissions because our analysts and external agencies shouldn't have access to the same customer data.
The event tracking API currently requires us to send events one at a time, which makes high-volume ingestion unnecessarily complicated.

data.text: We spend hours every week manually matching invoices with payments in QuickBooks. It's becoming a huge burden for our accounting team.

test_filter_task.text: We evaluated Datadog and Honeycomb but the per-seat pricing became painful for our 50-engineer team, so we ended up self-hosting.
How does ingestion cost compare to Grafana Cloud at your scale?
Last time we benchmarked it, Grafana's ingestion at our scale was about 3x cheaper than Datadog for the same cardinality.
nice
We had similar problems and ended up running Prometheus plus Grafana self-hosted on Kubernetes for our staging environment.
Prometheus storage got really expensive at our scale though, we ended up switching to Mimir for long term retention.
We use a custom Lambda that scrapes the AWS, GCP, and Azure cost APIs and writes everything to a single BigQuery table for analysis.
Have you tried Vantage? It centralizes cost data from multiple cloud providers into one dashboard.
How do you handle the granularity differences between providers when reconciling cost data?
We normalize everything to hourly granularity but it loses some of the per-request detail we needed for chargeback.
We had this exact problem at my last company and built an internal tool, but maintenance became a full-time job for someone.
Why not just use Cloudability? They support multi-cloud cost reporting out of the box.
I tried installing this today but the docs are unclear about the auth setup with our existing identity provider.
How does this compare to pyroscope for continuous profiling in production environments?
Same issue here. I ended up reading the source code to figure out how to configure oauth with our SSO provider.
We use this in production. The continuous profiling saved us hours of debugging last week during an incident.
What was the issue you were debugging? Curious about real-world wins from this tool.
lol
Cool project, bookmarked. I will try it on our staging cluster this week and report back.
The Notion API rate limits made it painful to sync our engineering docs automatically across multiple workspaces.
How did you handle full-text search across the migrated content from Notion to your new wiki?
Same problem at our company, our automation kept hitting 429s every few minutes and we would lose sync state.
yes
We considered Notion but the pricing for our 200-person company was hard to justify against self-hosted alternatives.
Curious what you ended up using instead? We are evaluating options for our own team right now.
Migration looked painful. How long did it take your team to move everything over to the new platform?
Every team I have worked on has built something like this internally. There should be a canonical open source solution.
What happens when a scheduled task crosses a DST boundary in a country that observes daylight saving?
It uses IANA tz database and stores everything in UTC internally, so DST transitions just work for cron expressions.
We built something similar and it broke every time a country changed their DST rules unexpectedly.
Yes, Egypt and Morocco both made last-minute changes recently and our scheduler broke silently for several days.
How does this handle leap seconds in scheduling? That has bitten us before with homegrown schedulers.

test_demand_object_task.text: Every sprint, our QA team spends about 2 days manually retesting features that were already covered by automated tests because our test coverage reports are unreliable.
GitHub Actions doesn't have a built-in way to chain workflows with conditional logic, so we ended up using a third-party orchestrator just to handle our release pipeline.
We have 14 different spreadsheets tracking customer support tickets across product lines, and we couldn't find a tool that integrates with all our helpdesk providers into one unified dashboard.
Jira's automation rules trigger way too many notifications. Half of my team has muted the channel entirely and now we miss critical alerts.
I built a custom Slack bot to summarize our 50 plus daily standups because the existing standup tools don't support our multi-team setup.
Our finance team wastes 6 hours every week reconciling payment data between Stripe, PayPal, and our bank statements, and none of those tools offer built-in reconciliation.
Linear does not support custom field workflows. We need to route issues to different teams based on a custom property, but Linear can't do that.
We migrated from Jenkins to GitHub Actions but the migration took 3 months because the existing Jenkins CI configuration was so complex and the tooling gap is large.
We have 200 plus microservices and no tool gives us a unified view of dependencies. We have been manually maintaining a dependency graph in Notion for two years.
Slack's search is essentially unusable once you have more than a few years of history. I end up scrolling through channels instead of searching for old messages.
I'd love a calendar tool that automatically blocks focus time based on my actual work patterns, not just heuristics like the existing calendar apps.
Our warehouse staff uses pen and paper to track inventory because our current WMS terminal app crashes every 30 minutes, and we are seriously considering switching vendors.
Postman doesn't handle our internal API authentication well. The token refresh logic in Postman breaks every time the auth server changes the TTL value.
Every quarter we spend 2 weeks manually preparing SOC 2 compliance evidence. The compliance tools on the market don't support our custom infrastructure setup.
I had to write a custom script to convert our Figma designs to Storybook stories because none of the existing Figma-to-Storybook plugins handle our design system tokens.
We use 6 different monitoring tools at our company and on-call engineers spend 30 minutes per incident figuring out which one to check first to debug the issue.
Notion's offline mode is unusable. Every time I open Notion on a plane, I have to wait 5 minutes for it to sync before I can edit any document.
We are evaluating Datadog but the per-host pricing is killing us at our scale. We process 20TB of logs per day and the Datadog bill keeps growing month over month.
Our product team needs a way to A/B test across web and mobile simultaneously. The existing experimentation tools treat web and mobile as separate experiments entirely.
I wish there were a simple tool for non-technical founders to set up basic GDPR compliance documentation, because every solution I have found is either too complex or too expensive.
